2: Serum IgG4 was elevated at 319 mg/dL (normal 4.8–105), with a normal total IgG of 1284 mg/dL (IgG4/IgG ratio 0.25).

Pituitary MRI demonstrated diffuse swelling of the pituitary body and stalk, a 7-mm poorly enhancing mass in the right anterior lobe, loss of the posterior pituitary bright spot on T1-weighted images, and thickening of the sphenoid sinus mucosa.
Given the combination of hypopituitarism, elevated IgG4 levels, and imaging findings, the patient underwent endoscopic transnasal surgery of the pituitary gland for definitive diagnosis.
